Hill-climbing medoid search on a shape distance matrix

Source: R/shape_medoid3d.R
shape_hill.Rd

Random-neighbor hill climbing for K medoids, ported from hill_climbing_shapes() of the 3D bagging scripts.

Usage

shape_hill(
  D,
  K,
  max_iter = 300L,
  from_best = FALSE,
  initial = NULL,
  distance = c("rho", "dF", "dP"),
  reflection = FALSE
)

Arguments

D

Numeric \(n \times n\) distance matrix, or a real landmark array \(k \times m \times n\), or a complex pre-shape matrix, from which distances are computed with distance.

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

max_iter

Number of neighbors tried (default 300, as in the scripts).

from_best

Logical. If FALSE (default), faithful to the script, each neighbor is a modification of the initial medoid set. If TRUE, each neighbor modifies the best set found so far, which is hill climbing in the usual sense.

initial

Optional vector of length K with initial medoid indices (1-based). If NULL they are drawn with sample.int().

distance

Distance used if D is not a distance matrix: one of "rho" (default), "dF", "dP".

reflection

Passed to shape_distance when D is a landmark array.

Value

A list with components:

cluster

Integer vector of length n, values in 1:K: the index of the nearest medoid.

medoids

Integer vector of length K, 1-based object indices.

objective

Sum of the distances of the objects to their nearest medoid.

n_iter

Number of neighbors that improved the objective.

distance

Distance name, or NA if D was a distance matrix.

Details

Starting from initial, each of the max_iter iterations replaces one randomly chosen medoid by a randomly chosen object, redrawing (cumulatively, on the same candidate set) while the set contains a repeated object, and keeps the candidate set if its objective is strictly lower. Objects are assigned with max.col()-style random tie breaking, as in the script, using R's generator, so for the same seed and distances the result equals that of the script.

In the script every neighbor is built from the initial set, never from the best set found, so it is a random search around the starting point and not a hill climb in the strict sense. This is the default so that results can be compared with the published scripts; from_best = TRUE gives the usual hill climbing.

See also

shape_pam, shape_clarans, bagclust1

Examples

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 10, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
D <- shape_distance(sim$X)
set.seed(1)
fit <- shape_hill(D, K = 2, max_iter = 100)
table(fit$cluster, sim$group)
#>    
#>      1  2
#>   1 10  0
#>   2  0 10
